definition: Incorrigible means incapable of being corrected or reformed.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word incorrigible. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know incorrigible should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Warnings, fines, and one towing later, the incorrigible double-parker was back astride the crosswalk by Friday.
A mischievous child makes playful trouble that one good scolding can end; incorrigible means the scoldings have stopped working and always will.
The wayward drift off course but can still be steered back; incorrigible is the far rung — the fiftieth correction lands exactly like the first.

Unreformable spells the claim out in plain parts — this person will not be reformed — and it stays grim, said of hardened offenders and broken institutions. Incorrigible makes the identical promise but often makes it smiling: the incorrigible flirt or punster is past fixing and half-loved for it.

Hopeless means beyond help of any kind, and no misbehavior is required — you can be hopeless at math or a hopeless romantic. Incorrigible is narrower and always about conduct: someone has tried, repeatedly, to correct this behavior, and the corrections will never take.
